races.name: Sports4Causes October Club EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Flexjet Pat Eddery Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Alfred Wallace
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy rides this Ed Walker-trained hold-up type who has already won over seven furlongs on Good ground and ran well in that company; his best hope is a strong pace that Sonny Parvenue alone may not provide.

runners_data.name: Dandyman Dan
runners_data.note: A dual winner who wants to race prominently, but with multiple speedsters seeking the same ground David Evans' colt will likely be squeezed into mid-division, which is against his natural grain; his two Good-ground efforts produced mixed results and 27 days off is not a concern.

runners_data.name: Firehorse
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partners this S Woods-trained debutant-turned-winner who arrives unbeaten after a six-furlong Sandown success; completely unexposed over seven furlongs, the step up suits on pedigree and a prominent tracking position is well within reach given the training angle.

runners_data.name: Gymbaazy
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows' OR=120 juvenile won over this exact seven-furlong Good-ground trip at Newbury, which is the most relevant piece of form in the race; Daniel Muscutt is a strong booking and the 42-day freshener rarely blunts this stable's juveniles.

runners_data.name: Kach Above
runners_data.note: Back-to-back seven-furlong wins at Goodwood are strong form claims for David Loughnane's filly, but she is naturally front-running or prominent by instinct and will find others blocking that path today; Laura Pearson takes a 3lb claim, which helps, but racing out of her comfort zone is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Silver Dominion
runners_data.note: Hector Crouch rides this Oliver Cole runner who scored on Soft ground over six furlongs and found only a rival too good over seven on Good ground last time; a prominent type that should get a reasonable position and the 13-day turnaround suggests the yard is happy with him.

runners_data.name: Sonny Parvenue
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's OR=120 debut winner over six furlongs on Good ground at Goodwood was visually impressive, and Pat Dobbs has confirmed front-runner intent; stepping up to seven is the only question, though Hannon's juveniles regularly progress with confidence over the extra furlong.

runners_data.name: Time For The Moon
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's hold-up performer won over this exact seven-furlong Good-ground trip at Goodwood before finishing tenth in stronger company; Billy Loughnane retains the ride and the horse's profile suits a truly-run race better than the patient tempo Sonny Parvenue is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Treasurer
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes' winner over six furlongs on Good ground arrives after a 24-day break and is effective when racing prominently, but with the pace map congested at the front, David Egan will likely find the colt running in a more restrained position than ideal; proven at six, seven furlongs is uncharted territory.

runners_data.name: Love Is
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes' filly won over six furlongs on Good ground and ran a solid second on Soft before finishing last on Good most recently; Finley Marsh rides and she carries 5lbs less than the top weights, which is a marginal assist, though being naturally prominent yet unable to access that position in this field is a structural disadvantage she must overcome.

races.paceDynamic: Sonny Parvenue is the confirmed front-runner and, on a flat Ascot seven-furlong straight, should stride into a clear lead from the outset with Pat Dobbs able to dictate his own rhythm without serious pressure. The going report confirms Good To Firm for this race, which rewards clean, forward-travelling horses and exposes any weakness in stamina at the trip's business end. Gymbaazy, Silver Dominion, and Firehorse are the prominent types most likely to actually secure their positions closest to Sonny Parvenue given their class and connections, while Dandyman Dan, Treasurer, Love Is, and Kach Above — all naturally prominent in style — cannot all claim that ground and will be shuffled into unfamiliar mid-division roles; this field carries significantly more speed than the track position can accommodate. With a sustainable, uncontested pace set by a single quality front-runner on fast ground, the shape strongly favours prominent-to-tracking types who can travel comfortably behind the leader, then quicken past in the final two furlongs — hold-up horses arriving late will likely find the winner gone.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sonny Parvenue Dictates Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Sonny Parvenue controls from the front unchallenged and the pace is metronomic enough that no prominent chaser can close the gap.
scenarios.body: Sonny Parvenue, trained by Richard Hannon and with a visually impressive debut win, sets a confident gallop and, never seriously pressed, stretches clear in the final furlong on the fast ground; Gymbaazy and Firehorse, locking onto his heels from prominent positions, fight out second and third.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Runs Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Gymbaazy or Firehorse travel strongly enough to collar Sonny Parvenue inside the final two furlongs as the pace picks up.
scenarios.body: Gymbaazy, unbeaten on Good ground at seven furlongs at Newbury and stepping up from a solid OR of 120, has the profile to stalk Sonny Parvenue and produce a superior finishing effort; Firehorse, a debut winner from S Woods, similarly carries unexposed upside that could overhaul the front-runner once the race ignites.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and leave the front end vulnerable to a late challenge from deep.
scenarios.body: Alfred Wallace, with proven Good-ground form at seven furlongs and the capable hands of Oisin Murphy, is the most credible hold-up beneficiary if the race burns fast enough to create late openings; Time For The Moon from the Charlie Johnston yard also has the profile of a horse capable of finishing powerfully, though both need more pace than Sonny Parvenue alone is likely to generate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Crowded Mid-Pack Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent types who cannot get their natural positions create interference and compress the mid-section, disrupting rhythm and producing a messy finish.
scenarios.body: With Dandyman Dan, Treasurer, Love Is, and Kach Above all forced into an unfamiliar mid-division role, traffic problems mid-race could compromise several fancied runners and promote a horse who finds daylight at the right moment; Silver Dominion, freshened by a 13-day break and tactically versatile, or Kach Above — back-to-back seven-furlong winners at Goodwood — could profit from the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Gymbaazy vs Sonny Parvenue is the central tactical duel — if Daniel Muscutt positions Gymbaazy directly on the leader's shoulder, his superior seven-furlong form on identical going makes him a serious danger to the front-runner inside the final furlong.

Monitor the early positions of Dandyman Dan, Love Is, Treasurer, and Kach Above — four prominently-styled horses fighting for limited tracking spots could create crowding and minor interference across the first two furlongs, affecting several runners' rhythms.

Firehorse is wholly unexposed and Tom Marquand rarely underperforms on big-occasion tracks like Ascot; as a single-run winner, her ceiling is genuinely unknown and she merits close watching if she travels smoothly in the first half of the race.

Alfred Wallace's chance is heavily conditional on pace — if Sonny Parvenue dictates a conservative tempo, Oisin Murphy will have little sprint to aim at and the hold-up profile is undermined; watch the early sectional to gauge whether the pace is hot enough to make him relevant late.

Time For The Moon's finishing tenth in a seven-furlong Goodwood Listed race on Good ground is a significant red flag — Billy Loughnane will need to produce a career-best to figure, and the watch point is whether the stable has found a specific reason for that poor effort.

races.name: John Guest Racing Brown Jack Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Synergism
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's four-year-old has solid similar-going form (three wins or places from five on comparable ground) and arrives 27 days fresh; the confirmed front-runner role at Ascot over two miles is exactly its comfort zone, though a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 flags a mild positional discount worth noting.

runners_data.name: Kirchner
runners_data.note: James Owen's gelding ran a strong second over 16f at Stamstead 27 days ago and Billy Loughnane's booking adds tactical quality; headgear flagged, and while similar-going form is limited (one win from six), Kirchner's natural prominence makes it the most likely horse to push Synergism.

runners_data.name: Fireblade
runners_data.note: A genuine front-runner by nature, Callum Rodriguez's mount arrives on a sharp 13-day turnaround with 12 good-ground runs in the bank; crowded out of its preferred spot by a field full of prominent types, it is mapped to midfield — a position that conflicts with its instincts — and the 17th-of-18 finish over 18f last time raises a distance query.

runners_data.name: Ghaiyya
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's four-year-old won over a mile and a half last time on good ground and has a tidy recent record, but bumped up to two miles with Jack Mitchell having to ride from the rear against its natural prominent style, the combination of trip doubt and position compromise makes this a guarded prospect.

races.paceDynamic: Synergism is the confirmed front-runner here and, in a field of just four, will be able to stride into a comfortable lead from the outset without any genuine pressure to accelerate early. Kirchner, Fireblade, and Ghaiyya are all naturally prominent types, meaning two of them are effectively displaced from their preferred position — Fireblade is mapped to midfield and Ghaiyya to the rear, but neither is a true hold-up horse, so the pace map overstates the depth of the chasing pack. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all get their position; Synergism and Kirchner are most likely to actually secure the prominent berths, with Fireblade and Ghaiyya forced wider or further back than they would ideally want. With Synergism allowed to control a steady gallop over two miles on good-to-firm ground at Ascot — a course that rewards horses travelling smoothly into the straight — the race shape strongly favours the horse that can dictate and sustain, making prominent-to-lead profiles the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Synergism Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Synergism is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a measured, even gallop the field cannot easily disrupt.
scenarios.body: Synergism takes the path of least resistance from the front, idles into the Ascot straight with petrol in the tank, and repels the chasing prominent horses whose natural rhythm has been compromised by the compressed field shape. Sir Mark Prescott's horses are notoriously well-prepared for their seasonal targets and the 27-day freshener fits the profile of a horse ready to confirm its form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Kirchner Tracks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Kirchner travels smoothly just off Synergism's shoulder and times a challenge from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Kirchner's most recent run was a fine second over 16f at Stamstead and Billy Loughnane can afford to sit a length or two off the leader before committing in the straight at Ascot. On good-to-firm, Kirchner's similar-going record of one win and one placed from six gives modest but real encouragement that the conditions suit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Fireblade Overcomes Displacement
scenarios.trigger: If Fireblade recovers from a compromised prominent position and picks up powerfully in the straight despite racing out of role.
scenarios.body: Dylan Cunha's charge arrives on just a 13-day turnaround and is a genuine prominent horse who has shown good form over 14f on good going, though the 18f flop last time raises a slight stamina question over this two-mile trip. The STYLE_FIT discount and redistribution to midfield make this a genuinely lower-probability shape, but Fireblade's recent course form over good ground keeps it live.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Ghaiyya Sweeps From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and Ghaiyya produces a strong sustained finish from well back.
scenarios.body: Ghaiyya is another naturally prominent type pushed to the rear by field congestion, so "closing from behind" is not a role this horse will relish — Charlie Johnston's runner won over 12f on good ground last time but the step to 16f-plus is unproven. The low probability reflects that Ghaiyya would be racing entirely against its instincts, and a race dominated by Synergism's controlled tempo is unlikely to set up the strong late finish this scenario requires.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Kirchner or Fireblade attempt to press Synergism early — if either challenges for the lead in the first half-mile, the gallop could quicken and blow the race wide open for hold-up types.
Fireblade's 13-day turnaround is tight for a two-mile Ascot handicap; watch the paddock for any sign of freshness or unsettled behaviour that might compound the positional problem.

Ghaiyya steps sharply up in trip from a mile and a half — watch how comfortably Jack Mitchell holds a position and whether the horse travels freely, as any pulling or resistance over early furlongs on fast ground will blunt the finish.

Synergism's trainer strike rate over 14 days is 3/13 — modest but not alarming; worth monitoring in-running whether James Doyle allows Synergism to coast or actively controls tempo, as a very slow early pace could compress the field and negate the front-runner advantage.

races.name: Sodexo Live! Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: French Duke
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner at OR 100 who won over 12f on good in recent form, wears headgear, and steps up to 1m4f on good-to-firm — the extra distance is a query but his ability to control the race is his main weapon; style fit noted as slightly out of role running prominently rather than outright leading here, which tempers confidence at a big price.

runners_data.name: Merveilleux Lapin
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows runner who shaped well for second on good ground over shorter trips, dropping back to hold-up tactics over a trip that stretches him — two wins out of five on similar ground is a modest hit-rate, and he needs a strong gallop to close from his position.

runners_data.name: Theory Of Tides
runners_data.note: Jamie Osborne's consistent performer has placed four times in eight similar-ground starts and Jamie's daughter Saffie takes the ride; races prominently and has the tactical versatility to sit just off French Duke, making her a key player if the pace is honest.

runners_data.name: Flying Frontier
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has been knocking on the door at OR 93 — four wins and six places in fifteen similar-ground outings reflects durability — but recent form of 19-844 over shorter trips raises questions about whether this trip on quick ground will unlock improvement or expose a flat spot.

runners_data.name: Dancing In Paris
runners_data.note: A genuine front-runner by instinct whose record includes second over 14f on soft and fourth over 16f, but with multiple prominent types ahead in the queue Ian Williams' charge is unlikely to secure a forward position naturally; the longer trip is on the positive side of the ledger, while the style compromise is a meaningful negative.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Believer
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners this nine-year-old who has zero wins and zero places in fifteen starts on good-or-faster ground — that statistic is a hard stop — but Ed Walker's recent form of 10/42 over fourteen days shows the stable in decent touch; the going is the clear concern.

runners_data.name: Al Azd
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's three-year-old is unexposed at this trip and carries a hood, with a form string of 221162 that reads as progressive; four wins and two places from nine similar-ground starts suggests he handles conditions, and racing prominently at OR 100 he has the profile of a horse likely to take a hand at the business end.

runners_data.name: Elsass
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's four-year-old ran just six days ago and is a natural hold-up horse who has won over 11f on good — though the quick turnaround and the likelihood of being held up wider than ideal in a prominent-heavy field are dual concerns alongside the style-fit discount.

runners_data.name: Study Of Words
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's lightly raced three-year-old steps up to 1m4f for the first time having won over 10f and placed over 14f, and Billy Loughnane takes over; 48 days since last run is the longest freshener in the field and the trip extension looks logical, making him an interesting hold-up type if the pace is genuine.

races.paceDynamic: French Duke is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only Theory Of Tides and Flying Frontier as genuine prominent types likely to press from the front, the pace at 1m4f on good-to-firm Ascot turf should be honest but not frantically contested — French Duke can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop without being seriously challenged for the lead. Al Azd is the other prominent runner with the form and class to sit close to the pace, meaning the first three or four positions will be occupied by horses happy racing forward, which shapes this into a race run at a fair rhythm rather than a dawdle. The hold-up contingent — Study Of Words, Merveilleux Lapin, and Fantasy Believer — will be racing from at least midfield and need either a strong enough tempo to create a stamina test or a decisive late surge to peg back those who control the race. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all get their natural position — Dancing In Paris and Elsass, though genuinely prominent and hold-up in style respectively, are mapped to midfield as they are unlikely to secure their preferred slots — and it is the horses who can sit third to fifth, travel smoothly, and sustain their effort through Ascot's long straight who are most favoured by this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Front Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If French Duke dictates a fair but unchallenging tempo and the prominent riders around him travel within themselves to the straight.
scenarios.body: French Duke sets a measured gallop that rewards those racing close to the pace, with Al Azd and Theory Of Tides poised to challenge as the field straightens up for home; the long Ascot straight becomes a sustained gallop rather than a sprint, rewarding class and stamina in the prominent berths.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Opens Closers Up
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent types — French Duke, Theory Of Tides, Flying Frontier, Al Azd — collectively push the pace hard enough to compromise their own finishing reserves.
scenarios.body: A genuine end-to-end gallop drains the prominent brigade and opens a clear lane for the hold-up horses sweeping through from midfield in the final two furlongs; Study Of Words and Merveilleux Lapin, both capable over this trip on similar ground, would be the chief beneficiaries of a true stamina test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Slow Early, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses early through lack of competition for the lead and the race turns into a late sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: French Duke slows proceedings to a near-crawl before the tempo suddenly lifts, compressing the field and reducing the advantage of stamina; prominent types with a turn of foot — Al Azd in particular given his form figures — are best placed to respond to the quick pace injection.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at an irregular rhythm with mid-race surges that cause bunching and leave the genuine hold-up horses without a clear run until very late.
scenarios.body: Fantasy Believer or Merveilleux Lapin might find daylight in a scramble to the line, though both have shown inconsistency in similar tactical scenarios and the redistributed Elsass — a true hold-up type squeezed for position — could also emerge late if gaps appear; this is the least likely shape given the field's composition.

watchPoints.text: French Duke's ability to control the tempo unchallenged is the single biggest race-shape variable — if Theory Of Tides or Flying Frontier press him hard from the start the whole dynamic shifts away from Scenario A.

Fantasy Believer's record of zero wins and zero places from fifteen starts on good-or-faster ground is a significant statistical flag — monitor market move and paddock condition closely before drawing conclusions from his prominent position in betting.

Elsass ran just six days ago and is a true hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield map position — watch for signs of fatigue or awkward positioning in the early stages that could compromise his run entirely.

Study Of Words steps up to 1m4f for the first time; if Charlie Appleby's yard have been working him specifically for this distance, the market move from his opening price will be telling given the trip is uncharted.

Al Azd's headgear (blinkers noted) and progressive form make him one to track in the paddock — if he travels smoothly in the first half of the race and is sitting third or fourth into the straight, he is the horse most likely to dictate the finish under the Scenario A shape.

races.name: Chapel Down Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Walson's Law
runners_data.note: Won a 7f handicap on Good ground recently and boasts a strong record in similar conditions (6 runs, 2 wins, 3 placed); prominent style suits this pace shape well, and Eve Johnson Houghton's yard is firing at 8/31 over 14 days — a live contender to track Mr Writer and pounce late.

runners_data.name: Havana Blue
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up performer with a fine recent record at 7f on Good, including a runner-up finish at that trip; Julie Camacho's team only 1/15 in the past fortnight, but Callum Rodriguez takes over and the horse's tactical versatility allows him to sit closer than his typical style if needed.

runners_data.name: Gallant
runners_data.note: Consistent at 7f on Good ground but the sim-going record (0 wins, 0 placed from 6 similar runs) raises doubts about converting proximity into victory; headgear (t) worn and the step back from 8f should sharpen him, though Oli Rix is a small yard and Tom Marquand will need luck from a busy field.

runners_data.name: Independent Expert
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up specialist whose recent form is littered with mid-field finishes; six runs on Good ground have yielded zero wins or places, and the shortish gap since his last run (4 days) is a minor concern for a hold-up horse who will need things to unfold perfectly from the back.

runners_data.name: Dapper Guest
runners_data.note: David Egan rides a horse who has finished 13th in his only recent Ascot run at this trip; the sim-going record (1 win, 1 placed from 10) is acceptable but the form string (-08640) suggests he is currently out of form and the hood (v) hasn't sparked a revival yet.

runners_data.name: Mr Writer
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter and the critical shape-setter for the whole race; wins his two 7f Good-ground starts from the front and the STYLE_FIT tag (0.90) relates to him being pushed into a slightly different tactical context, but here he is in his natural lead role — the key question is whether the handicapper has caught him.

runners_data.name: H Key Lails
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose last win came over 7f on Good and who has placed at 8f on Tapeta; headgear (p) worn and a 5lb claimer (Seamus Cronin) in the saddle is a meaningful weight relief, with the trainer quiet (0/5 in 14 days) but this horse's profile fits the race shape well enough to be dangerous.

runners_data.name: Be Frank
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose natural station is off the pace — though mapped closer here, he is unlikely to secure a midfield berth in practice; the form string (6545-6) is uninspiring, the layoff (42 days) needs to be navigated, and the STYLE_FIT tag reflects the compromise his true racing pattern faces in this configuration.

runners_data.name: Illy's Roo
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who won her only 8f start on Good but has placed nowhere in five subsequent 7f attempts; jockey Kaiya Fraser is an apprentice, and while the drop back to 7f that suits her winning style, the form line is thin enough to make this a race-to-learn exercise rather than a winning pitch.

runners_data.name: Mystic Moment
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is an obvious positive, but this three-year-old's natural closer style is compromised by the crowded hold-up section; pushed into midfield on the map, he is more likely to race from the rear in reality, and his recent efforts (37-658) show a horse yet to reproduce his early-season placed effort.

runners_data.name: Wield
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old who was placed at 7f on Good going and placed twice at Wolverhampton; the 70-day absence is the big concern, and while his natural come-from-behind style puts him in the same redistribution crunch as several rivals, Wield has enough raw ability to make the frame if the pace accelerates mid-race.

runners_data.name: King Of War
runners_data.note: Won a 7f Good-ground contest recently and has placed five times at similar tracks; the headgear (tp) is retained, and although his true hold-up style is squeezed into a midfield berth by the sheer number of closers in this field, he has demonstrated a finishing kick that becomes relevant only if the pace genuinely quickens.

runners_data.name: Tex
runners_data.note: Career record shows five places without a win on Good ground, and the 58-day absence for a horse rated 67 in a field with plenty of class above him makes a winning performance unlikely; his honest, consistent profile (33-230) suggests he will run his race, but the redistribution context means he cannot get his natural position and that compounds his challenge.

races.paceDynamic: Mr Writer is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner handicap over Ascot's 7f, and with no genuine rival likely to push him hard early, he should be able to dictate at a sustainable gallop rather than a pressured one. Walson's Law and Gallant will press from prominent positions, while H Key Lails and Havana Blue will track just off the pace, meaning a small group will race keenly enough to set up a proper test without turning it into a sprint. The pace shape here is honest but not fierce — a single-figure front-runner controlling tempo over Ascot's straight 7f on Good to Firm ground typically rewards those able to track close to the action and pounce in the final two furlongs rather than those coming from the rear. This field holds significantly more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate in their natural positions: Wield, Mystic Moment, Be Frank, King Of War and Tex are all true come-from-behind types who are mapped to midfield but will likely find themselves further back than ideal, diminishing their realistic chance of making a winning challenge. The tactical verdict favours prominent racers who can sit just off the pace-setter and exploit the final-furlong stamina premium that Ascot's 7f demands.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Pace Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Writer dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the field strings out behind him.
scenarios.body: Mr Writer, unharassed from the front, sets fractions comfortable enough to sustain his effort deep into the straight, making it very difficult for those rearward to close the gap on the Good to Firm surface. Horses tracking him closely — Walson's Law, Gallant, H Key Lails — are best placed to mount the only credible challenge as the lead is never truly cut back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is brisk enough to test Mr Writer but not so fierce that it collapses the field into chaos.
scenarios.body: A genuine but measured gallop set by Mr Writer sees him caught inside the final furlong by a prominent tracker who has conserved energy; Walson's Law's strong form at 7f on Good ground makes her the chief beneficiary, with Havana Blue capable of swooping from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace accelerates sharply mid-race and the front runners tire in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A quicker-than-expected tempo burns off Mr Writer and the prominent horses, leaving a gap for a closer to finish strongly through beaten rivals; Wield and Illy's Roo are the most likely beneficiaries, though both face the challenge of navigating traffic on a straight track with limited natural room.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses to a crawl early and the race turns into a sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A false-pace scenario sees the race bunched entering the straight, negating Mr Writer's positional advantage and opening the race up to anything with a sharp turn of foot; King Of War's recent 7f win on Good ground gives him strong claims, while Tex's placed record on similar surfaces makes him a viable each-way interest.

watchPoints.text: Mr Writer has set the pace in every win — if he is tracked aggressively early by Walson's Law or Gallant and asked to go faster than his comfort zone, he may empty in the final furlong and hand the race to a closer.

Wield (70 days off), Be Frank (42 days off) and Tex (58 days off) are all returning from significant breaks — watch how they travel early for signs of race-rustiness; any who hit a flat spot at the two-furlong pole are unlikely to rally on Good to Firm ground.

The field contains at least five genuine hold-up horses (Wield, Mystic Moment, Be Frank, King Of War, Tex) all likely to be further back than their mapped positions — watch for traffic problems and interference entering the final two furlongs as they all seek the same running rail.

H Key Lails carries a 5lb claimer allowance with Seamus Cronin — watch whether that weight advantage allows him to sit closer to Mr Writer than his recent form might suggest, as the combination of claim and prominent style in this pace shape makes him a price-sensitive runner.

Going reports have consistently described the 7f course as Good to Firm all afternoon — watch for any late watering update before the off, as several prominent runners (Walson's Law, Mr Writer) have their best form on Good rather than quicker ground and a firming surface tilts the shape further in favour of the front-runner.

races.name: Sodexo Live! Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Toolatetonegotiate
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will be sent straight to the lead under Oliver Carmichael; unbeaten when making all over 5-6f at Ascot and in similarly good going, though the style-fit tag suggests she is unlikely to be allowed a completely uncontested transit with this field.|

runners_data.name: Lady Roxby
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a disappointing recent run of 7s at 6f suggesting the drop to 5f and fast ground could be the key to revival; trainer Herrington hit 1/8 in the 14-day window and 6f form on similar going is limited, so the trip shortening is a significant unknown.|

runners_data.name: Killavia
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up filly handled by Oisin Murphy whose single win came over 5f on Good ground; strong course-relevant form at this trip gives her a solid profile, but from the rear she needs the pace to be honest and a clear passage.|

runners_data.name: Paradise Walk
runners_data.note: In-form prominent filly carrying the hood and recording back-to-back wins including over this exact course and distance; Ralph Beckett's yard is firing at 12/43 in the 14-day window and Hector Crouch's positive ride style suits a horse who wants to travel handy.|

runners_data.name: Lara Antipova
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has placed in three of four starts and handles Good to Firm well; David Egan will look to slot her into the first three early, though the step up in class at Ascot is the main question mark on just four career starts.|

runners_data.name: Desert Treasure
runners_data.note: William Haggas filly who has won two from two over 5f on fast ground but her true style is prominent and she has been redistributed to midfield because the race cannot accommodate all the pace-seeking types; Tom Marquand will try to recover the lost position but traffic risk is real.|

runners_data.name: Dandy Magic
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly returning just four days after her last run, which demands scrutiny; her Good-to-Firm record at 6f has been poor (3/15 sim-going) and she has never won, making her profile one of the weaker ones regardless of race shape.|

runners_data.name: Carefree Dream
runners_data.note: Neat hold-up performer with two placed efforts over 5f on similar ground; JF Egan has the tactical awareness to find a position, and her form figures of 2-2 over 5f on Good are the most relevant, though she has yet to win and the OR of 70 sets the ceiling.|

runners_data.name: Fantasy Obsessor
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up filly whose true preference is for being held up late, but redistribution means she may be forced forward earlier than ideal; Saffie Osborne takes the ride on a visor-wearing mare who has finished second three times recently without landing a blow, and the STYLE_FIT tag tempers expectations.|

races.paceDynamic: Toolatetonegotiate is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should be able to control tempo from the off on this flat Ascot 5f. Desert Treasure and Fantasy Obsessor are natural prominent and hold-up types respectively but the field is congested with pace-hungry runners, meaning both are likely to be shuffled away from their preferred positions — Desert Treasure in particular cannot rely on getting the prominent berth she wants. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate cleanly; Paradise Walk, Lady Roxby and Lara Antipova will all be pressing for the early positions behind Toolatetonegotiate, compressing the midfield and creating a bunched, competitive break. On Good to Firm ground over a flat 5f at Ascot, a single, uncontested leader setting a genuine but manageable pace hands a clear tactical edge to prominent racers who can track and pounce in the final furlong — the pace scenario therefore most favours those able to sit just behind the leader and produce a sustained finish without needing a dramatic switch in track position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Toolatetonegotiate Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Toolatetonegotiate leads uncontested and the chasing pack travels smoothly just off the pace on Good to Firm ground.
scenarios.body: Toolatetonegotiate sets a controlled, honest gallop and the field strings out naturally; prominent runners sat two to three lengths off the pace are best placed to reel her in through the final furlong on fast ground where kicks are sustained rather than explosive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On, Brave Front
scenarios.trigger: If Toolatetonegotiate is allowed an even softer lead than expected and the prominent pack fails to coordinate a timely challenge.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing to press early, Toolatetonegotiate builds a rhythm and the flat track offers no undulation to catch her out; hold-up runners are caught flat-footed and the front-runner's stamina proves sufficient over the minimum trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the multiple prominent types jostle for position and burn pace early, leaving the race wide open in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A scrappy break with several fillies competing for the first two or three spots creates a faster-than-expected early tempo, draining the principals; a genuine hold-up filly with a clear run benefits from the resulting late meltdown.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Winner Emerges Wide
scenarios.trigger: If significant crowding and traffic issues at halfway force multiple horses to switch wide, handing initiative to one who finds space cleanly.
scenarios.body: The compression of prominent types seeking their positions causes interference mid-race; the horse that finds a clean lane soonest on the outside turns the race into a sprint to the line from two furlongs out.

watchPoints.text: Paradise Walk's back-to-back winning form over this exact course and distance makes her the most dangerous pursuer if she secures a prominent pitch behind Toolatetonegotiate — watch whether Hector Crouch gets her into a smooth rhythm by the two-furlong pole.

Desert Treasure's redistribution to midfield is the key tactical hazard — Tom Marquand will attempt to push forward from her mapped position and if she creates a surge near the stands rail in the opening furlong it could compromise several runners beside her.

Dandy Magic's four-day turnaround combined with a weak Good-to-Firm record and zero career wins flags a potential non-runner-quality runner who could still cause interference if she dwells or hangs under pressure from a cramped midfield position.

Killavia represents the most credible threat from off the pace, but Oisin Murphy must find clean air from a hold-up position in a 9-runner 5f field — watch her positioning at the two-furlong mark as any traffic there ends her chance immediately.

The Going Report confirms Good to Firm for this race despite the card header showing Good — fast ground will place a premium on clean early position and any horse slow to load or break will find itself with too much ground to make up on the flat Ascot straight.
